reviews.justification: The registry already asks for referral to early developmental intervention services under the global developmental delay unit, which is the same decision retrieval never proposed.
Nothing in the myopathy unit addresses surveillance for complications, but the row names no specific complication, so the reasoning target is not single.
Arranging specialist follow-up here is service navigation with no named clinical trigger and would not anchor a single-best-answer item.
Resuscitation of unstable early-pregnancy bleeding sits inside the broad management row already carried by this unit.
The Indigenous health coverage and jurisdictions unit already carries system-navigation reasoning about split jurisdictional responsibility.
Rhythm interpretation is part of the bundled syncope risk-stratification row rather than a separately enumerated decision.
Routine wound-healing reassessment is ordinary follow-up care rather than a discriminating decision for a graduating student.
Verifying donation consent status is handled through provincial donation organizations and sits beyond entry-level supervised practice.
Oral versus intravenous rehydration is explicitly enumerated in the pediatric dehydration and gastroenteritis units under different wording.
Repeat neurovascular checks fall within the concrete systematic hand-examination row this unit already carries.
Radiographic surveillance of talar fracture union is orthopedic follow-up detail rather than an entry-level decision.
Notifying a donation coordinator is an administrative handoff that no single-best-answer item would test at this level.
Distinguishing occupational from non-occupational causation is already enumerated in the occupational history unit.
Ordering a complete blood count for possible anemia is covered by the abnormal uterine bleeding workup rows.
Selecting isolation precautions is already enumerated in the infection prevention and control unit.
Perioperative risk disclosure is carried by the preoperative consent row, and the row as written pairs two different audiences.
Informed consent for an intervention is enumerated in the consent and capacity unit rather than in the immunization unit.
Arranging specialist support for dementia is service navigation without a named clinical trigger.
Analgesic selection for acute injury is already enumerated in the acute pain management unit.
Management and referral for sexual dysfunction is carried by the gynecology unit, and the referral trigger is left unspecified.
Recognition of subconjunctival hemorrhage is bundled into the existing benign conjunctival lesion row for this unit.
Longitudinal imaging surveillance for post-traumatic osteonecrosis belongs to orthopedic follow-up practice.
Identifying hemodynamic instability is contained within the broad diagnosis and management rows for first-trimester bleeding.
Emergency resuscitation of severe pediatric dehydration is enumerated in the dedicated dehydration unit.
Deciding to refer grief that has become prolonged or unsafe is a distinct scoreable decision the bereavement unit never enumerates.
This row states a documentation style preference about form numbering rather than a clinical decision with a determinate best answer.
Referral for specialized obstetric planning is stated without a decision threshold and reads as service navigation.
Initiating involuntary assessment once the legal threshold is met is bundled into the existing threshold-recognition row.
Generic psychosocial surveillance in chronic neuromuscular disease has no determinate best answer at this level.
Choosing muscle biopsy for tissue diagnosis is a subspecialty investigation decision beyond entry-level practice.
Arranging occupational support for dementia is a service-coordination task rather than an assessable clinical decision.
Advising driving or work restriction after unexplained syncope is a distinct Canadian safety decision absent from this unit at any granularity.
Referral pathways for persisting functional symptoms are unenumerated, but the row names no specific care target.
The normal-versus-pathologic row already covers this discrimination, and the row asks for both reassurance and return advice.
Explaining that functional symptoms are real and mechanistically explainable is a core communication decision this unit never enumerates.
Separating syncope from seizure is enumerated in the cardiac loss-of-consciousness differential unit.
Immobilizing an injured hand is a discrete initial management decision that this unit covers only for triage and examination.
Direct hemorrhage control belongs to the trauma resuscitation unit rather than to the interventional radiology procedures unit.
Coaching caregivers away from accommodating avoidance is a specific, scoreable counselling decision missing from the pediatric anxiety unit.
Psychosocial contributors to poor growth are enumerated in the failure-to-thrive unit.
Tracking functional decline in myopathy is generic chronic-care monitoring with no determinate single answer.
Medical contributors to poor growth are enumerated in the failure-to-thrive unit.
Reassessing hand function during rehabilitation is routine follow-up rather than an assessable decision point.
Consent or lawful substitute decision-making is enumerated in the consent and capacity unit rather than the ECT unit.
Mandatory reporting of a notifiable infection is enumerated in the public health reporting unit.
A dedicated shoulder dystocia unit exists in the registry and was never proposed as a candidate.
Establishing injury timing is part of the bundled triage row for traumatic hand injuries.
Resuscitating uncontrolled hemorrhage belongs to the trauma and shock units, not to the interventional radiology unit.
Non-judgmental sexual history taking is bundled into the existing screening row and is a manner of interviewing rather than a discrete choice.
Recognizing developing infection at a reassessment visit after hand trauma is a discrete decision this unit does not enumerate.
Anticipating osteonecrosis as a consequence of talar fracture is a distinct complication-recognition decision absent from the unit.
Activity restriction duplicates the immobilization decision and is stated without a specific indication.
Disposition and follow-up flow directly from the existing syncope risk-stratification row.
Choosing intrapartum fetal surveillance is enumerated in the fetal monitoring in labour unit.
Arranging community supports for dementia is service coordination rather than a scoreable clinical decision.
Urgent escalation of unstable first-trimester bleeding is contained in the existing management row and duplicates the resuscitation row.
The row bundles two different explanatory contents with no single response to score.
Providing longitudinal continuity is a care-organization expectation rather than a decision with a best answer.
Ensuring personnel capable of neonatal resuscitation are present for a meconium-stained delivery is a discrete decision absent from this unit.
Culturally attentive physical comfort care sits inside the broad end-of-life assessment and communication rows and names no single response.
Counselling to reduce recurrence of urinary infection is a distinct preventive decision the urology unit does not enumerate.
Reading a positive prenatal screen as altered risk rather than a diagnosis is a discrete interpretive decision the unit does not enumerate.
Establishing injury mechanism is part of the bundled triage row for traumatic hand injuries.
Treating pain at end of life is enumerated in the palliative pain and symptom management unit.
